dev_result: 22/26, 4 kernel-config-buffer overflow at K=V=128 and K>V

what: No guidance on the kernel-config-buffer (program text) limit: a large fused compute kernel fits in production but overflows by 2-4 KB under --dev (watcher+LLK asserts). Outlining helpers (noinline), loop-folding and pragma unroll caps mostly made TRISC images larger because the LLK reconfig/init state tracking is only elided at compile time when inlined; KernelBuildOptLevel is not exposed in ttnn Python (only under fabric_mux) and O2 breaks LLK immediates.
suggest: Document the per-core kernel text budget, how --dev inflates it, which levers actually shrink TRISC code (dedupe call sites of heavy SFPU ops; not noinline), and that --dev overflow is a size limit not a correctness failure.
